title: session-ontology-exploratory-notes
content:
TL;DR: brainstorm for a lightweight session ontology that lets apps model multi-layered context (persistent user profile, ephemeral memory, task scopes, and plugin state) with an API that keeps inference costs predictable and privacy-preserving. Goal is an incremental, opt-in surface that developers can adopt for richer assistants without blowing up token budgets or runtime latency.

Motivation / Problem space:
- Many customers want "memory" for assistants but have different needs: some want a long-lived persona, others want per-task scratchpads, and most want session resume behavior but bounded cost.
- Current approaches conflate everything into a monolithic session history; that makes caching ineffective and causes unpredictable token spikes.
- Need a canonical, small set of primitives (layers) so downstream systems (batching, caching, routing) can reason about requests.

Core concept: Layers (very rough)
- persistent_profile (pinned by user): small structured + freeform fields, user-controlled, encrypted at rest, TTL optional
- task_scope (per-workflow): ephemeral named blob, intended to survive for N hours or until explicitly cleared
- recent_turns (sliding window): compressed token stream for immediate context (kept short, default 512 tokens)
- plugins_state (opaque): plugin-specific key-value store, namespaced by plugin id
- signals (structured): meta flags like "high_priority", "billing_tier", "qa_mode"

Properties we want:
- explicit size / token budget for each layer (configurable per-app)
- layer-level read/write API (no need to stream entire session)
- deterministic eviction policy (LRU, TTL, pinned) + metadata for why eviction happened
- versioned schema for layers to allow model-aware upgrades
- strong opt-in semantics and per-layer consent markers for privacy/compliance

Developer API sketches (proto):
- POST /sessions -> creates session id + base config
- PATCH /sessions/:id/layers/:layerName -> upsert structured or blob content (small payloads only)
- GET /sessions/:id/layers?names=... -> fetch subset (for cheap warmups)
- POST /sessions/:id/compose -> returns a composed prompt bundle (layers + recent_turns) trimmed to token budget
- Headers / params: X-Token-Budget, X-Preferred-Latency-SLO, X-Persist: true/false

User stories (prioritized):
- As a product engineer, I want to attach a small persistent_profile with name + preferences so the assistant can greet the user consistently without re-sending the whole history.
- As an app developer, I want the ability to create a task_scope that survives across failures so background workers can resume a conversation.
- As an ops engineer, I want the platform to expose per-layer token accounting and eviction events so I can tune budgets and observe regressions.
- As a privacy officer, I want per-layer consent flags and an audit log for reads/writes to satisfy compliance.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API supports 3 layer types (persistent_profile, task_scope, recent_turns) with documented size limits.
- Compose endpoint trims and orders layers according to a deterministic policy and returns metadata: token_estimate, trimmed_layers[].
- Telemetry emitted for: layer_reads, layer_writes, compose_token_estimate, eviction_reasons.
- End-to-end latency impact: additional 95th percentile <= 10ms for reads under normal ops (goal <=5ms).
- Storage: encrypted at rest; retention configurable per layer; default retention 30 days for task_scope, 365 days for persistent_profile (customer configurable).

Rollout/experiment plan:
- Alpha: internal feature flag for a small set of production customers (10 orgs), read-only 'compose' API so we validate prompt composition and token estimates without changing stored state.
- Beta: enable write APIs with per-org quotas and observable eviction events. Run A/B on latency and cost.
- GA: expose to self-serve with tiered defaults (free tier: small persistent_profile only; paid: task_scope + larger budgets).

Telemetry / metrics to track:
- avg tokens per compose (by customer and endpoint)
- percent of composes that trimmed >=1 layer
- per-layer read/write qps and p50/p95 latency
- storage growth per-org and projected monthly cost
- number of eviction events per session per day

Open questions / risks (non-exhaustive):
- Schema vs freeform: How much structure to force? Too much and we limit use cases; too little and platform can't optimize caching. Maybe provide a small canonical schema for persistent_profile with optional freeform blob.
- Cost model: Charging per-read? per-store? If we store lots of small layers it can still blow up operational cost. Need heuristics to compress and dedupe across sessions (fingerprinting).
- Encryption/E2E: customers want encrypted fields — do we offer envelope encryption where keys are customer-managed? Impacts search/composition features.
- Cross-device sync: should be responsibility of app or platform? Likely platform provides durable storage + optional websockets for sync, but scope creep.
- Eviction UX: how do we signal to app that an important piece was evicted? Need metadata and hooks for pre-eviction snapshot.

Implementation sketch (engineering notes):
- Storage: metadata + small blobs in a tiered store. Hot cache (redis/memcached) for active sessions; cold store (tiered object store) for less-active persistent_profile.
- Indexing: per-org LRU keyed by session_id:layer_name. Support approximate counting for cost projections.
- Compose step should run in the same request path as inference for simplest upgrade path but we can pre-compose in a sidecar for heavy apps.
- Compression: use gzip + simple token-preserving compaction (sentence-level heuristics).

Privacy & compliance checklist (initial):
- per-layer consent flag + audit log (who read/wrote, when)
- ability to purge all layers for a user (GDPR right to be forgotten) within 24h SLA
- KMS integration for envelope encryption for enterprise/private customers
- redaction pipeline for PII on write (configurable per-layer)

Prototyping tasks (next steps):
1) Build a simple in-process model: local layer store + compose endpoint; integrate with hosted-api call path for read-only compose. Measure typical token budgets from 10 pilot apps. (owners: Ishaan + Drew)
2) Wire telemetry in a lightweight way: events for layer_reads/writes and compose token estimate. Hook into Console dashboards (owner: Marta).
3) Draft API docs + playground snippets for front-end prototypes (owner: Evelyn).
4) Security review checklist and initial conformance doc for product legal (owner: Noah).

Notes to self / random ideas:
- Consider a "named snapshot" primitive which is an immutable composed snapshot of layers at a point in time; useful for retries and deterministic evals.
- Might be useful to expose composer hints to models (e.g., mark some fields as "system" vs "user-preference") to improve model conditioning and reduce hallucination.
- Explore cheap semantic indexing for persistent_profile to dedupe similar entries across sessions.

Outstanding dependencies / tickets to create:
- JIRA-PS-8722: implement compose endpoint prototype
- JIRA-PS-8723: telemetry schema and Console panel
- JIRA-SEC-481: encryption + redaction requirements
- GH: draft proto + integration test harness (PR#97 referenced above)

Questions for product sync:
- Which three customers should we target for alpha? (recommend: two chat-heavy SaaS apps + one internal infra tool)
- Default budgets by tier? propose: free: 1KB persistent_profile, 256 token recent_turns; paid: 10KB persistent_profile, 1024 token recent_turns, task_scope allowed.
- Back-compat: how to migrate customers who already store long histories in session? Provide a migration helper that slices history into "recent_turns" + fingerprinted persistent_profile.

End of notes. This is intentionally rough — want to validate the assumptions with a few partner teams before turning into a formal PRD.
